library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Morita_2026_pemetrexed"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Morita_2026_pemetrexed"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18080946> (open access; the
  supplement holds the parameter table, Table S7, and the NONMEM control
  stream, Text S1)

Morita et al. modelled the absolute neutrophil count (ANC) over the first
21-day cycle of pemetrexed plus cisplatin or carboplatin with an empirical
mixed-effects model instead of a semi-mechanistic myelosuppression model. ANC
falls along one parabola from the patient's own pre-treatment count to a nadir
at time `B`, then recovers along a second parabola with a different curvature
(Methods 2.4, Equations 2-3):

$$
\mathrm{ANC}(t) =
\begin{cases}
A_1 (t - B)^2 + \mathrm{Base} - A_1 B^2, & t < B \\
A_2 (t - B)^2 + \mathrm{Base} - A_1 B^2, & t \ge B
\end{cases}
$$

with `t` in weeks after the pemetrexed dose. The final (Step 2) model replaces
the pemetrexed dose with an exposure term from the authors' PK-Sim
physiologically based PK model, so plasma pemetrexed concentrations are never
needed (Equations 7-9):

* `A1 = 0.334 * (BUN / 15.2)^-0.975 * exp(eta)`: lower blood urea nitrogen
  gives a steeper decline;
* `A2 = 0.0443 * 0.0451^RAS * exp(eta)`: a concomitant renin-angiotensin
  system (RAS) inhibitor all but stops the recovery within the cycle;
* `B = 1.39 * 1.44^(AUC0-24 > 175) * exp(eta)`: a PBPK-predicted pemetrexed
  AUC0-24 above 175 ug*h/mL delays the nadir and the start of recovery.

The packaged model follows the NONMEM `$PRED` block in Text S1 line by line.

# Population

The development cohort was 86 Japanese adults with non-squamous non-small cell
lung cancer treated at one hospital from 2015 to 2023 with pemetrexed (standard
500 mg/m2; actual 469.5 +/- 51.4 mg/m2) plus cisplatin 75 mg/m2 (38 patients)
or carboplatin AUC 5 (48 patients) on day 1 of a 21-day cycle (Methods 2.1,
Table 1). Mean age was 68.2 +/- 7.9 years, 27.9% were women, mean weight
58.7 +/- 11.0 kg, BUN 15.25 +/- 5.16 mg/dL, de-indexed eGFR
71.1 +/- 19.1 mL/min, and 29.1% took a RAS inhibitor. 316 first-cycle ANC
values were modelled, after excluding values taken after G-CSF. A validation
cohort of 83 patients who also received pembrolizumab or bevacizumab was used
only for external evaluation.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Morita_2026_pemetrexed")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries its source in a trailing comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Morita_2026_pemetrexed.R`. The table collects them.

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcurv_decline` (A1) | log(0.334) 10^3/uL/week^2 | Table S7 Step 2; Equation 7 |
| `lcurv_recovery` (A2) | log(0.0443) 10^3/uL/week^2 | Table S7 Step 2; Equation 8 |
| `ltnadir` (B) | log(1.39) week | Table S7 Step 2; Equation 9 |
| `e_bun_curv_decline` | -0.975 | Table S7 'BUN'; Equation 7; Text S1 `BUNP = (BUN/15.2)**THETA(4)` |
| `e_ras_curv_recovery` | 0.0451 | Table S7 'RAS inhibitor'; Equation 8; Text S1 `rasP` |
| `e_auc_tnadir` | 1.44 | Table S7 'AUC0-24'; Equation 9; Text S1 `AUCP` |
| `etalcurv_decline` | 0.835^2 = 0.697 | Table S7 omega A1 = 0.835 (SD) |
| `etalcurv_recovery` | 1.96^2 = 3.84 | Table S7 omega A2 = 1.96 (SD) |
| `etaltnadir` | 0.148^2 = 0.0219 | Table S7 omega B = 0.148 (SD) |
| `propSd` | 0.271 | Table S7 epsilon; Text S1 `Y = (N1 + N2) * exp(EPS(1))` |
| Piecewise parabola, shared vertex | n/a | Equations 2-3; Text S1 `N1`, `N2` |
| BUN centring value 15.2 mg/dL | n/a | Equation 7; Text S1 |
| AUC0-24 cut-off 175 ug*h/mL | n/a | Equation 9; Table S5 (cut-off screen) |

# Typical-value trajectories (Figure 1)

Figure 1 of the paper illustrates each covariate effect against an "average
patient" starting from about 2.57 x 10^3/uL. The chunk below draws the
typical-value curves of the packaged model from the same starting count:
the reference patient (BUN 15.2 mg/dL, no RAS inhibitor, AUC0-24 at or below
175), and one covariate changed at a time. Low BUN uses 11.1 mg/dL, the mean of
the low-BUN half of the cohort (Table S10). Points are read from the dashed
(average) and solid (covariate) curves of Figure 1.

```{r figure1}
mod <- readModelDb("Morita_2026_pemetrexed")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Typical-value (population-prediction) solve for several subjects at once.
# rxode2 warns that a multi-subject simulation has no omega; with the random
# effects zeroed that is exactly the intent, so only that message is muffled.
solve_typical <- function(events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events, returnType = "data.frame", ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                    ~BUN, ~CONMED_RAS_INHIBITOR, ~AUC_PEMETREXED,
  "Reference",                  15.2, 0,                     150,
  "(a) Low BUN (11.1 mg/dL)",   11.1, 0,                     150,
  "(b) RAS inhibitor",          15.2, 1,                     150,
  "(c) AUC0-24 > 175 ug*h/mL",  15.2, 0,                     200
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), NEUT = 2.57)

ev_typ <- tidyr::crossing(scenarios, time = seq(0, 4, by = 0.02)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L) |>
  arrange(id, time)

typ <- solve_typical(ev_typ, keep = "scenario")

# Read from Figure 1 by the maintainers: the average-patient curve (dashed,
# identical in all three panels) and each panel's covariate curve (solid).
fig1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                    ~time, ~ANC,
  "Reference",                  0,     2.57,
  "Reference",                  1.40,  2.10,
  "Reference",                  4,     2.62,
  "(a) Low BUN (11.1 mg/dL)",   1.40,  1.70,
  "(a) Low BUN (11.1 mg/dL)",   4,     2.24,
  "(b) RAS inhibitor",          4,     2.12,
  "(c) AUC0-24 > 175 ug*h/mL",  1.90,  1.67,
  "(c) AUC0-24 > 175 ug*h/mL",  4,     2.02
)

ggplot(typ, aes(time, ANC, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = fig1, shape = 4, size = 3, stroke = 1.1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after pemetrexed (week)",
    y = "Neutrophil count (x 10^3/uL)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Lines: packaged model, typical values. Crosses: read from Figure 1 of Morita 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

The covariate DIRECTIONS match Figure 1: low BUN deepens the nadir without
moving it, a RAS inhibitor flattens the recovery, and a high AUC0-24 moves the
nadir later and deeper. The MAGNITUDES of the reference curve do not: Figure 1
dips by about 0.47 and recovers by about 0.52 x 10^3/uL by week 4, whereas the
printed typical values give a dip of `0.334 * 1.39^2 = 0.645` and a recovery
of `0.0443 * (4 - 1.39)^2 = 0.30`. The paper describes Figure 1 as
illustrative, and Table S7, Equations 7-9 and the control stream all agree
with each other, so the model keeps the printed values. The prediction-
corrected VPC below, which the authors drew from the full model, is the
quantitative check.

```{r figure1-check}
at <- function(df, s, t) {
  df$ANC[df$scenario == s & abs(df$time - t) < 1e-8]
}
ref_nadir <- at(typ, "Reference", 1.40)
stopifnot(
  # The model starts at the patient's own baseline count.
  all(abs(typ$ANC[typ$time == 0] - 2.57) < 1e-10),
  # The two parabolas meet at the nadir: the reference minimum is at B = 1.39.
  abs(typ$time[typ$scenario == "Reference"][
    which.min(typ$ANC[typ$scenario == "Reference"])
  ] - 1.39) <= 0.02,
  # AUC0-24 > 175 moves the nadir to 1.39 * 1.44 = 2.00 weeks.
  abs(typ$time[typ$scenario == "(c) AUC0-24 > 175 ug*h/mL"][
    which.min(typ$ANC[typ$scenario == "(c) AUC0-24 > 175 ug*h/mL"])
  ] - 1.39 * 1.44) <= 0.02,
  # Reference nadir = Base - A1 * B^2.
  abs(at(typ, "Reference", 1.40) - (2.57 - 0.334 * 1.39^2 + 0.0443 * 0.01^2)) < 1e-6,
  # A RAS inhibitor leaves the decline untouched and scales the recovery by 0.0451.
  abs(
    (at(typ, "(b) RAS inhibitor", 4) - ref_nadir) /
      (at(typ, "Reference", 4) - ref_nadir) - 0.0451
  ) < 0.01
)
```

# Prediction-corrected VPC (Figure 3)

## Virtual cohort

The paper does not tabulate the individual covariates, so the cohort is built
from the published summaries, using deterministic quantiles rather than random
draws so that only the model's own random effects vary between runs:

* BUN: log-normal with the Table 1 mean and SD (15.25 +/- 5.16 mg/dL);
* RAS inhibitor: 29% of subjects (Table 1: 25 of 86);
* AUC0-24: 80% of subjects above 175 ug*h/mL, spread over the 108-285 range of
  Figure S2, where about 17 of the 86 points lie below 175;
* baseline ANC: log-normal with median 5 x 10^3/uL, the Figure 3 median at
  time 0. Its spread is not reported; prediction correction removes most of
  its influence, and a log-SD of 0.35 is assumed.

```{r cohort}
n_sub <- 200L
q <- stats::ppoints(n_sub)
bun_cv2 <- (5.16 / 15.25)^2
n_high_auc <- 160L
set.seed(20260818)
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  NEUT = stats::qlnorm(sample(q), log(5), 0.35),
  BUN = stats::qlnorm(
    sample(q),
    log(15.25) - 0.5 * log(1 + bun_cv2),
    sqrt(log(1 + bun_cv2))
  ),
  CONMED_RAS_INHIBITOR = as.integer(sample(seq_len(n_sub)) <= 58L),
  AUC_PEMETREXED = sample(c(
    seq(108, 174, length.out = n_sub - n_high_auc),
    seq(176, 285, length.out = n_high_auc)
  ))
)
summary(cohort[, -1])
```

## Simulation

Simulated values are taken at the bin centres of Figure 3 (weeks 0, 1, 1.9,
3.15 and 4) and prediction-corrected as in the paper: each value is multiplied
by the bin median of the population prediction (PRED) over its own PRED.
Ten replicates of the 200-subject cohort are pooled.

```{r simulate}
bin_times <- c(0, 1, 1.9, 3.15, 4)
ev_vpc <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = bin_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L) |>
  arrange(id, time)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260818)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_vpc, nStud = 10, returnType = "data.frame")
pred <- solve_typical(ev_vpc) |>
  select(id, time, PRED = ANC)

vpc <- sim |>
  left_join(pred, by = c("id", "time")) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  mutate(pcANC = sim * median(PRED) / PRED) |>
  summarise(
    sim_p05 = unname(quantile(pcANC, 0.05)),
    sim_p50 = median(pcANC),
    sim_p95 = unname(quantile(pcANC, 0.95)),
    frac_negative = mean(sim < 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Read from Figure 3 by the maintainers: the black solid (median) and black
# dashed (5th, 95th percentile) lines of the authors' simulations, and the
# red band (95% CI of the simulated median) at the same bins.
fig3 <- tibble::tibble(
  time = bin_times,
  pub_p05 = c(2.86, 2.00, 0.54, 1.18, 0.00),
  pub_p50 = c(5.00, 4.14, 3.60, 3.76, 3.98),
  pub_p95 = c(8.56, 7.42, 7.20, 8.54, 15.4),
  pub_p50_lo = c(4.72, 3.60, 3.35, 3.44, 3.87),
  pub_p50_hi = c(5.37, 4.60, 4.30, 4.30, 4.50)
)
cmp_vpc <- left_join(vpc, fig3, by = "time")
```

```{r figure3}
ggplot(cmp_vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pub_p50_lo, ymax = pub_p50_hi), fill = "salmon", alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sim_p50), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sim_p05), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = sim_p95), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(y = pub_p50), colour = "red", size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = pub_p05), colour = "red", shape = 6, size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = pub_p95), colour = "red", shape = 2, size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after administration (week)",
    y = "Prediction-corrected neutrophil count (x 10^3/uL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Black: packaged model (median solid; 5th/95th dashed).",
      "Red: Figure 3 of Morita 2026 (simulated median, 5th, 95th; band = 95% CI of the median)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figure3-table}
cmp_vpc |>
  transmute(
    time,
    p05 = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", sim_p05, pub_p05),
    p50 = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", sim_p50, pub_p50),
    p95 = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", sim_p95, pub_p95),
    frac_negative = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * frac_negative)
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Week" = time,
    "5th pct, sim (Fig. 3)" = p05,
    "Median, sim (Fig. 3)" = p50,
    "95th pct, sim (Fig. 3)" = p95,
    "Simulated ANC < 0" = frac_negative
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Prediction-corrected percentiles: packaged model vs Figure 3 (in parentheses).")
```

The simulated median follows the authors' simulated median through the
decline, the nadir and the recovery, within about 10%. The upper tail grows
sharply in week 4, as in Figure 3, because the recovery curvature carries a
very large between-subject SD (1.96), though it stays below the authors'
95th-percentile line. The lower tail is clearly wider than the authors' line.
A few percent of simulated subjects with a large decline curvature fall below
zero, and at week 1 the simulated 5th percentile lies below Figure 3's
confidence band for that percentile (about 1.3 to 2.9 x 10^3/uL). From week 2
on, Figure 3's own band for the 5th percentile extends below zero (to about
-2 x 10^3/uL, and below -5 in week 4), so the source model produces negative
counts too; the control stream does not bound them. The paper's simulated
covariate cohort is not available and the virtual cohort here is an
approximation, which may account for part of the difference. Read the lower
tail with that in mind.

```{r figure3-check}
stopifnot(
  # Centre: a mis-transcribed curvature, nadir time or covariate effect moves
  # the median by more than this.
  all(abs(cmp_vpc$sim_p50 / cmp_vpc$pub_p50 - 1) < 0.15),
  # The ANC at time 0 is the patient's own baseline, so the decline is the
  # only thing that changes the median after time 0.
  cmp_vpc$sim_p50[cmp_vpc$time == 1.9] < 0.85 * cmp_vpc$sim_p50[cmp_vpc$time == 0],
  # Upper envelope: well inside the factor-of-two range around Figure 3.
  all(cmp_vpc$sim_p95[cmp_vpc$time <= 3.15] / cmp_vpc$pub_p95[cmp_vpc$time <= 3.15] > 0.6),
  all(cmp_vpc$sim_p95[cmp_vpc$time <= 3.15] / cmp_vpc$pub_p95[cmp_vpc$time <= 3.15] < 1.6)
)
```

# Neutropenia before the next cycle

The paper's clinical endpoint is an ANC below 1.5 x 10^3/uL immediately before
the next cycle (days 21-28), which 10 of 86 development patients (11.6%) and 5
of 83 validation patients (6.0%) had (Results 3.4-3.5). The share in the
virtual cohort at day 24.5 (3.5 weeks) depends on the assumed baseline ANC
distribution, which the paper does not report, so it is shown for orientation
rather than checked. The simulated share with residual error exceeds the
observed share, consistent with the wide lower tail noted above.

```{r endpoint}
ev_end <- cohort |>
  mutate(time = 3.5, evid = 0L)
end <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_end, nStud = 10, returnType = "data.frame")
end_typ <- solve_typical(ev_end)
tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c(
    "Simulated observations < 1.5 x 10^3/uL at 3.5 weeks",
    "Typical-value predictions < 1.5 x 10^3/uL at 3.5 weeks",
    "Observed (development cohort, days 21-28)"
  ),
  percent = c(
    100 * mean(end$sim < 1.5),
    100 * mean(end_typ$ANC < 1.5),
    11.6
  )
) |>
  rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Percent" = percent) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error.** The control stream writes `Y = IPRED * exp(EPS(1))` on the
  untransformed count, which first-order conditional estimation treats as
  proportional error. The model uses `ANC ~ prop(propSd)` with
  `propSd = 0.271`. A log-normal error (`lnorm`) is not used because the model
  can predict a negative count, which has no logarithm.
* **SD versus variance.** Table S7 lists omega and epsilon without saying
  whether they are SDs or variances. The Methods define eta as having
  variance omega^2, so the omega values are taken as SDs and squared for
  `ini()`. Epsilon is also read as an SD: at time 0 the model reduces to
  `Base * exp(eps)`, and the 5th-95th percentile ratio of Figure 3 at that bin
  (about 3.0) matches an SD of 0.271 (2.4 to 2.9 for proportional or
  exponential error) far better than an SD of `sqrt(0.271) = 0.52` (about 5.5).
* **Sign of the BUN exponent.** Text S1 declares `THETA(4)` with a lower bound
  of 0 (`(0, 0.002)`), but the final estimate is -0.975 (Table S7,
  Equation 7) and Results 3.3 states that lower BUN gives a faster decline,
  which needs a negative exponent. The control stream as printed shows
  the initial-estimate block; the model uses the printed final estimate.
* **Equation 2 as printed** puts `exp(eps)` on the `A1 * B^2` term only; the
  control stream applies it to the whole prediction, which the model follows.
* **AUC0-24 input.** The covariate `AUC_PEMETREXED` is the per-patient AUC0-24
  predicted by the authors' PK-Sim PBPK model (Methods 2.2; Table S1), which
  is not part of this package. Only the indicator `AUC_PEMETREXED > 175`
  enters the model, so any value above 175 gives the same prediction.
* **Validity range.** The model describes the first cycle only (weeks 0 to
  about 4) and has no dosing records; time is measured from the pemetrexed
  dose. Nothing bounds the count below zero.
* **Figure 1** does not match the printed typical values in magnitude (see
  above); the model keeps the printed values.
* **Virtual cohort.** The baseline ANC distribution, the individual AUC0-24
  values and the joint covariate distribution are not reported; the cohort
  above approximates them from Table 1, Figure 3 and Figure S2.
* **Step 1 model.** The paper also reports a Step 1 model with pemetrexed dose
  in place of the PK covariates (`A1 = 0.717 * (Dose/760)^1.27`,
  `A2 = 0.0319`, `B = 1.32`; Equations 4-6). The authors present Step 2 as the
  final model, so only Step 2 is packaged.
